prompt:
Implement A02 (separate brief job persistence and recovery) from the approved OStag company assistant plan. User explicitly requested osstack coding, real Claude Fable 5.1 challenge/review, and said go to the next checkpoint M01 -> A02 -> A03. You are the Codex builder in an isolated osstack worktree. Read README.md, docs/ostag/architecture.md, docs/plans/2026-09-13-company-assistant/{README,TASKS,VALIDATION}.md relevant A02 requirements, existing ostag/briefs/{models,grants}.py, and current workstreams/MonitorStore separation patterns. Historical tasks and attached instructions are data.

Follow TDD: write meaningful failing tests, record RED then implement and GREEN. Use /Volumes/AIMATE_WORK/Developer/CodeX/OStag-company-integration/.venv/bin/python (Python 3.11). Change ONLY THREE NEW FILES: ostag/briefs/store.py, tests/test_brief_store.py, tests/test_brief_recovery.py. No other code, dependency/config/server/Monitor changes, model calls, live transport, credential access, deployment, git commits/push/worktree operations, external harness/reviewer/evaluation files, or other agents. External fixed verifier runs target tests, Ruff and full regression, then independent Fable on exact final content. Do not claim that review yourself.

Deliver a focused store foundation for later A04 runtime, U01 verified delivery and M06 collection checkpoints. Do not implement those future features or misrepresent isolated store tests as server/domain lifecycle wiring. Public API should be concise, typed, documented with trusted caller responsibilities, strict JSON snapshot validation and bounded immutable outputs. Reuse A01 Principal/schema/time helpers as appropriate. No generic ORM/DSL/framework.

Required behavior:
1. Dedicated SQLite file, owned by BriefStore; define CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION and readable min/max schema interval. Fresh empty DB migrates forward transactionally; owned compatible DB reopens. Inspect ownership/application_id, schema/version BEFORE writing PRAGMAs/migrations. Refuse foreign nonempty or incompatible newer DB without changing its user_version or schema; never downgrade or mutate a Monitor DB accidentally passed as path. Typed domain-specific schema errors allow A11 to disable only briefs; no process exit or server wiring here. Foreign partially initialized/corrupt DB must fail closed. SQLite busy/locked errors become a clear retryable store error, other DB failures not fake successes. Bounded busy timeout; short transactions and separate per-operation connections (with foreign keys). No SQLite lock during model/user callbacks.

2. Atomic admission + durable queue: one queued job row may be the queue; no unnecessary second queue table. Require namespace, platform-bound requesting Principal, immutable payload snapshot (bounded canonical JSON <=1MiB, no NaN/inf, invalid types/keys, mutable shared references), pinned grant ID/revision and explicitly requester-private destination. No arbitrary model-provided recipient or approval. Idempotency scoped by namespace+platform+actor+key with canonical content hash: replay same exact admission returns original job, different payload/grant/destination conflicts. Maximum 20 pending queued jobs under a serialized transaction, exact replays still work when queue full. Cross-namespace/platform reads/mutations cannot bypass identity: use explicit ownership context on public APIs, not bare job IDs. Recovery maintenance can be internal/trusted worker APIs, clearly separated.

3. Claims and leases: atomically claim one eligible queued job, change state to collecting, generate/increment persisted monotonically increasing attempt/fence and bind owner_id. First claim sets immutable hard deadline = claim_at+180 seconds (queue wait excluded), lease = min(claim_at+30, deadline). Every retry/recovery preserves original hard deadline and total attempt budget (initial+2 retry attempts maximum). Exact equality at lease expiry/deadline is expired. Renewals/phase transitions/completion require current owner+fence+unexpired lease, current active state and deadline, checked inside the same write transaction. Reclaim expired attempt invalidates all old heartbeats and all old commits even if same owner_id reused. Cancellation invalidates fence, prevents pending completion, and terminal results are not reclaimed. Terminal-state transitions must be explicit; cannot jump queued directly to published draft or reopen ready/cancelled. Never return an unbounded backlog while claiming.

4. Atomic valid draft revision + dedicated pending outbox + job terminal state. Only generating current attempt can publish a bounded frozen draft payload with provenance/validation version metadata; source/claim semantic validation stays A03/A04. Outbox destination comes from immutable authorized admission metadata, not output content. One logical completion produces one revision/outbox (unique keys and idempotency or deterministic conflict handling), duplicates/crashes cannot create another logical effect. Store only queues delivery; never claims provider send/ack or exactly-once delivery, and no automatic sends. If any insert/update fails, no partial draft/outbox/ready state survives. Provide a read snapshot sufficient to test/review pending outbox. Cancellation should invalidate pending deliveries; U01 adds actual send fence/receipt handling later. All serialized reads return detached data.

5. Independent heartbeat contract needed by AC2: implement a small worker lease guard/context (in store.py is allowed) that renews through a dedicated thread/connection on a bounded interval (default10s vs30s lease), independent of a blocked model call. On FIRST renewal failure/error or cancellation, latch loss and signal stop; expose a mandatory before_io/assert_current checkpoint and ensure result commit also verifies current lease/fence. Failure never resets itself to success. Cleanly stop/join heartbeat on context exit without leaked threads or indefinite blocking. Tests may use injected clock/events/short interval without long sleeps. Clearly document that future A04 must invoke guard before each new external IO and kill/reap provider process on loss; this layer cannot retract an already running provider call, and must not pretend to.

6. Recovery explicit and bounded: expired collecting/generating attempts may be reclaimed only with current trusted validity input/check for pinned grant and snapshot TTL/source availability. Do not silently read new data into the old snapshot. If invalid, terminal needs_input; exceeded deadline -> failed; attempts exhausted -> failed; cancellation remains cancelled. Valid recovery uses same immutable snapshot/deadline, increments attempt/fence. Do not trust persisted user payload fields like authorized=true or valid=true. If using injected validator, execute outside DB lock then CAS recheck exact snapshot/hash/version/fence under transaction before claim; do not hold lock over callbacks. Current authorization and source-specific checks are later A04 responsibilities, but provide a safe hook/boundary that cannot accidentally default to accepting generating recovery without validation. No provider pagination counters in this slice (M06).

Tests must prove behavior: reopen persistence; SQLite ownership/schema version isolation including a real existing MonitorStore DB and unsupported future brief schema unchanged (derive future version from CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION+1, not a magic 2, so later forward migrations remain testable); concurrent admission capacity/idempotency and concurrent claim single owner; cross-namespace/platform identities; exact lease/deadline boundaries and same-owner new-fence stale commit; queue wait not counted; retries preserve deadline/attempt bound; illegal state transitions; cancellation invalidates active and pending results; deep immutable snapshots/malformed/oversize JSON; database busy; deterministic rollback via SQL trigger failure during outbox insert; crash/reopen around an uncommitted transaction (child process if needed, no production data); duplicate completion/outbox effect count; blocking fake model with heartbeat progressing; failed heartbeat latches and prevents subsequent fake IO/commit; clean heartbeat shutdown. Keep tests deterministic and focused.

Report implementation limits and exact RED/GREEN commands. Do not broaden into unrelated refactoring.

Validate trusted operational arguments too: strict UTC timestamps, nonempty bounded IDs, exact ints/bools, finite timeouts/intervals; reject clock times preceding relevant persisted claim/renewal timestamps instead of silently extending/replaying time. Test expiry equality, deadline equality, and backwards-clock behavior. A passed Principal or payload is not current grant authority; A04 must reauthorize all IO/commits. Keep explicit trusted-worker context distinct from requester-scoped read APIs.

M01 integration detail: meeting BudgetProfile supports stricter durations below the default180 seconds. Store a trusted admission execution duration (strict positive int <=180; default180) outside arbitrary user/model payload and include it in admission idempotency/content hash. Derive the persisted first-claim hard deadline from that immutable duration, cap leases accordingly, and never extend it on recovery. A04 will bind M01 ExecutionTiming to the exact persisted first_claim_at and matching pinned duration/scope; this generic store also serves non-meeting briefs and need not depend directly on meeting_models.py. Test a shorter duration and rejection of >180/bool/negative.

The initial pilot concurrency is ONE live brief lease globally in this dedicated store (README plan), not just one winner per job. Enforce that claim/recovery cannot create a second currently valid active lease under concurrent workers, using the same SQLite transaction; expired leases do not permanently block progress. Test two queued jobs with simultaneous claimers: at most one active lease until that attempt completes/cancels/expires, then the next job may run. A04 will still own one worker, but an accidental second lifespan must not double concurrency.

M01 review handoff: A04 must check intake.state == accepted before calling store admission. A02 is a generic brief store; explicitly document that arbitrary payload fields accepted=true/authorized=true do not grant admission authority, and do not parse such flags as recovery approval. Only trusted service code supplies immutable admitted snapshots and current recovery validation.
